steps.explanationAfterStep: One concerted step through a 'butterfly' transition state. Both C–O bonds form on the same face of the alkene, so the alkene's geometry is kept in the epoxide (syn addition). The leaving group is a stable carboxylic acid.

title: Epoxidation of cyclohexene
subtitle: mCPBA delivers one oxygen in one step
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 19

reactants.caption: cyclohexene + mCPBA (Ar = 3-chlorophenyl)
hintTiers: The O–O bond is weak. Which oxygen ends up in the epoxide: the one bonded to H, or the one bonded to the carbonyl carbon?

The OH oxygen bonds to both alkene carbons. Go round the ring: the O–H bond becomes one C–O bond, the C=C π bond forms the other, the O–O bond becomes a new C=O, and the old C=O takes the H. Four arrows, in any order.

Arrow 1: from the O–H bond to one alkene carbon, forming a C–O bond. Arrow 2: from the C=C π bond to the same oxygen, from the other alkene carbon. Arrow 3: from the O–O bond to between the carbonyl carbon and the oxygen next to it. Arrow 4: from the C=O π bond to the H.
reactants.learnerPrompt: mCPBA transfers one oxygen to the alkene in a single step. Draw all the arrows.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The alkene attacks the far end of the O–O bond, the oxygen carrying the H. The oxygen next to the carbonyl group becomes part of the new C=O.
The C=O oxygen is not electrophilic. The alkene attacks an oxygen of the weak O–O bond.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right start. Keep going round the ring: the C=C π bond to the same oxygen, the O–O bond to a new C=O, and the old C=O to the H. Four arrows in all.

mechanismSummary: In one concerted step the alkene π bond attacks the terminal oxygen of the peroxy acid, the weak O–O bond breaks to form the new C=O, the old C=O takes the proton, and the O–H electrons form the second C–O bond. Both C–O bonds form on the same face (syn addition): cyclohexene oxide and m-chlorobenzoic acid.
